_meta.note: Regression reference for Meeting Hijack Stopper (renamed from Meeting Hijack Preventer, 2026-09-03, the day after the plan-first rewrite). The v1 golden was discarded rather than ported: its single case exercised an endpoint that no longer exists and its expected output contained speaking roles, meeting artifacts and a success-metrics string the rewrite removed. Re-run with `npm run check:golden meeting-hijack-stopper` against a local backend and diff for QUALITY, not exact match. Beyond what check-golden asserts automatically, eyeball these by hand, because no gate sees them: (1) nothing may describe a participant's personality, motive or feelings — a selected challenge is a facilitation problem, never a claim about a person; (2) nothing may invent decision authority, an escalation path, or an exact lead time such as 'send it 24 hours in advance'; (3) no ritual should appear (ground rules, icebreakers, round robins, parking lots, formal roles, Tech Support) unless it solves a problem in that specific meeting; (4) the agenda is fitted to the duration DOWNWARD only, so unscheduled_minutes > 0 is correct behaviour, not a bug. Each case carries its own `guards` line saying what it is there to catch. See audit/tool-notes/MEETINGHIJACKSTOPPER-NOTES.md.

cases.name: plan-decision-unknown-authority
cases.guards: Framework is 'Not sure', so decision_plan.what_needs_clarifying MUST name who decides rather than inventing an answer, and no escalation path may appear. Two challenges → exactly two watch_for. scheduled_minutes + unscheduled_minutes == 60; the agenda is fitted DOWNWARD only, so slack the model left is slack it meant.

input.meetingGoal: Decide which two of the four proposals move forward to the design phase.
input.extraContext: Two of the proposals came from the same team and they are invested in both.

meeting_plan.goal: Decide which two of the four proposals move forward to the design phase.
meeting_plan.end_state: Two proposals are selected and written down with a clear record of the choice, or the unresolved selection and the person or process with authority to settle it are clearly identified, along with whatever partial agreement was reached.

agenda.title: Clarify the decision and who can make it
agenda.purpose: Establish upfront how two proposals will be chosen and who has authority to finalize it, so the rest of the meeting has a clear endpoint.
agenda.how_to_run_it: Name the decision plainly: which two proposals advance. Ask the group directly whether there is an agreed process for making that call, and who has authority if the group cannot reach agreement. Write the answer where everyone can see it before moving on.
agenda.say_this_if_helpful: Before we get into the proposals, I want to make sure we know what we are deciding and how. We need to choose two of the four proposals to move forward. Does everyone understand that framing? And if we cannot reach agreement, who has the authority to make the final call? I want that settled now so we are not figuring it out at the end.

agenda.title: Brief review of each proposal
agenda.purpose: Give every participant a shared baseline on all four proposals before evaluation begins.
agenda.how_to_run_it: Give each proposal roughly four minutes. Ask whoever is presenting or summarizing it to cover the core idea and what advancing it would require. Hold questions until all four have been introduced.
agenda.say_this_if_helpful: We will take about four minutes per proposal to make sure everyone has the same picture. Please hold questions until we have been through all four.

agenda.title: Identify the strongest cases for each proposal
agenda.purpose: Surface the reasoning behind each proposal so the group is comparing on substance, not just preference.
agenda.how_to_run_it: Open discussion, but actively manage airtime. For each proposal, invite arguments in its favor and any significant concerns. If discussion stalls on one proposal, move it forward. If it runs long, redirect to the next. Note that two proposals share a team of origin; invite the group to assess all four against the same criteria rather than treating origin as a factor.
agenda.say_this_if_helpful: For each proposal, I want to hear the strongest case for advancing it, and any material concerns about doing so. We will try to apply the same lens to all four. We have about five minutes per proposal, so I will move us along when needed.

agenda.title: Select two proposals or frame the unresolved choice
agenda.purpose: Reach the decision or, if agreement is not there, produce a clear and actionable statement of what is unresolved.
agenda.how_to_run_it: Ask whether any two proposals have clear support from the group. If yes, name them and confirm. If there is disagreement, identify exactly which proposals are in contention and what the sticking point is, then apply the decision process clarified in the first block.
agenda.say_this_if_helpful: Based on what we have heard, I want to see if we can name two proposals. Are there two that the group feels ready to move forward? If there is disagreement, let us be specific about which proposals are in question and what is making this difficult.

watch_for.situation: One person speaks at length on most points, and other voices are not getting into the discussion.
watch_for.prevent_it: State early that you will be actively inviting other perspectives throughout, so it is expected rather than surprising when you do.
watch_for.if_it_happens: Redirect by name to the group, not to the individual, to avoid making it personal.
watch_for.say_this: I want to make sure we hear other perspectives on this before we move on. Is there anything we have not covered yet?

watch_for.situation: The conversation moves away from which two proposals advance and onto broader topics such as implementation details, team resourcing, or future phases.
watch_for.prevent_it: Write the decision question visibly at the start and refer back to it whenever discussion drifts.
watch_for.if_it_happens: Name what is happening and redirect to the decision in front of the group.
watch_for.say_this: That is worth exploring, but it is going to pull us away from the choice we need to make today. Can we note it and come back to the two proposals?

decision_plan.approach: The first agenda block establishes how the group will decide and who has authority if agreement is not reached. The discussion in the middle blocks builds a shared picture of each proposal. The final block uses that shared picture to test for agreement on two proposals. If agreement is present, name the two proposals and record them. If the group cannot agree, name exactly which proposals are in contention, what the sticking point is, and refer the unresolved choice to whoever was identified as having authority in the first block.
decision_plan.what_needs_clarifying: Who has the authority to make the final selection if the group does not reach agreement. This is not established and should be named in the first agenda block before discussion begins.

before_the_meeting: Send participants a short summary of all four proposals with enough time to review before the meeting, so the review block can stay brief.
Prepare a shared visual or document where you can write the decision question, any agreements, and open items as the meeting runs.
Know in advance whether the two proposals from the same team will be presented by that team, and plan to apply consistent criteria across all four regardless of origin.

before_people_leave: If two proposals were selected, write them down and confirm the group sees the same record.
If the selection is unresolved, write the exact question that remains open and name which proposals are in contention.
Record whatever partial agreement was reached, even if the final choice was not settled.
Name who has authority to settle any unresolved choice and what the next step is.
Confirm whether any follow-up communication is needed and who will send it.
finish_strong.closing_script: Here is where we landed: either two proposals are confirmed to move forward, or we have a clear picture of what is still open and who will resolve it. I will make sure that record goes out to everyone so we are working from the same information. Thank you for the time.

cases.name: plan-names-supplied-disagree-and-commit
cases.guards: The case the 2026-09-03 pass exists for. Names ARE supplied, so using them is allowed — but nothing may RANK them (no 'the three most directly affected', no 'key stakeholder'), and 'Dana will be affected' must stay exposure rather than becoming a constraint Dana holds: 'ask Dana how the splits would affect the platform group', never 'get Dana's constraints'. 'Disagree & commit' is a discussion norm, not authority: with no decision owner established, no script may demand a yes or a no, require anyone to commit, or declare anything final. end_state must carry BOTH branches — a split agreed, OR the unresolved question and its decision owner identified — because an outcome that only counts when the room agrees is an outcome for half the meetings. before_people_leave must work either way. And the previous unresolved quarter is context, not a mandate: 'the meeting's stated goal is to settle it today', never 'we cannot let that happen again'. All three watch_for entries must describe what someone in the room would SEE — two people speaking at once, an agreement still vague about the next action — never heat, defensiveness or private lack of commitment.

input.meetingGoal: Agree how we split on-call between the two teams for next quarter.
input.participantNotes: Sam and Priya lead the two teams. Dana runs the platform group and will be affected.
input.extraContext: The two teams disagreed about this last quarter and it was never resolved.

meeting_plan.goal: Agree how on-call will be split between the two teams for next quarter.
meeting_plan.end_state: A specific on-call split for next quarter is agreed and written down, or the exact unresolved choice and the person or process that can settle it are clearly identified.

agenda.title: Frame the problem and the finish line
agenda.purpose: Orient everyone to the same question so the discussion has a clear target from the start.
agenda.how_to_run_it: State the goal plainly: leave with a decided split or a clear decision path. Name the two possible endings so no one is surprised if agreement is not reached. Invite Sam and Priya to confirm the question is framed correctly before discussion opens.
agenda.say_this_if_helpful: Last quarter this stayed unresolved. Today the goal is to leave with a clear on-call split for next quarter, or if we cannot get there, a clear statement of what is unresolved and who can settle it. Sam, Priya, does that capture what we need to decide?

agenda.title: Surface the options
agenda.purpose: Get the realistic split options on the table before anyone argues for one, so the discussion is about choices rather than positions.
agenda.how_to_run_it: Ask Sam and Priya to each describe what they see as workable splits, one at a time without interruption. Write each option where everyone can see it. Then ask Dana how the proposed splits would affect the platform group. Do not editorialize; just capture.
agenda.say_this_if_helpful: Before we debate anything, I want to get the options visible. Sam, what splits seem workable from your side? I will capture it, then Priya, I will come to you.

agenda.title: Examine the options
agenda.purpose: Work through the practical trade-offs of each option so the group has enough information to move toward a choice.
agenda.how_to_run_it: Take each option in turn. Invite the group to raise practical concerns or questions about it. Keep discussion on observable factors: coverage, load, handoffs. If the conversation drifts, name the option you are on and bring it back. If one voice is carrying the whole discussion, explicitly invite other perspectives before continuing.
agenda.say_this_if_helpful: Is there anything we are missing before we move to the next one? We have not heard from everyone yet.

agenda.title: Move toward a decision
agenda.purpose: Turn the discussion into a concrete choice.
agenda.how_to_run_it: Ask whether there is an option, or a combination, the group can live with. If one emerges, state it clearly and check for objections. If a genuine objection is raised, ask what would need to change for it to be workable. If no agreement is in reach, name the sticking point precisely and ask who in the room, or outside it, has the authority to make the final call.
agenda.say_this_if_helpful: We have about ten minutes. Is there an option on the board, or a version of one, that everyone can work with? If there is a real objection, let us hear it now.

agenda.title: Lock down what we are leaving with
agenda.purpose: Ensure the outcome is concrete enough to act on whether or not the group fully agreed.
agenda.how_to_run_it: Read back exactly what was decided, or exactly what remains unresolved. Assign a named next step and owner for anything not settled. Confirm who will communicate the outcome and to whom.
agenda.say_this_if_helpful: Let me read back what we are leaving with so we are all working from the same thing.

watch_for.situation: One person is speaking for an extended stretch and other voices have not come in.
watch_for.prevent_it: Name the expectation early: you will be moving between perspectives to make sure the group has the full picture before deciding.
watch_for.if_it_happens: Cut in at a natural pause, acknowledge the point briefly, and redirect by name to someone who has not spoken.
watch_for.say_this: I want to bring in some other perspectives before we stay with this one. Who else has a view on this option?

watch_for.situation: The discussion moves away from the on-call split and onto a different problem or grievance.
watch_for.prevent_it: Write the specific question on a shared surface at the start so it stays visible as an anchor.
watch_for.if_it_happens: Name the drift without judgment and redirect to the decision in front of the group.
watch_for.say_this: That is worth discussing, but I do not think we can do it justice here. Can we note it and come back to the split question?

watch_for.situation: Two people start talking at the same time and one thread risks getting lost.
watch_for.prevent_it: Establish at the start that you will manage speaking order when it gets tangled.
watch_for.if_it_happens: Name both speakers, pick one to go first, and commit to returning to the other.
watch_for.say_this: Let us take these one at a time. Sam, finish your point, then Priya, I will come straight to you.

watch_for.situation: The clock is running short and the group is still working through options without a decision in sight.
watch_for.prevent_it: Flag the time at the start of the decision block so urgency is shared, not just held by the facilitator.
watch_for.if_it_happens: Name the time remaining, state the two possible endings, and ask the group to choose which path they are on.
watch_for.say_this: We have about five minutes. If we are not going to land a decision today, I need us to name exactly what is unresolved and who can settle it.

watch_for.situation: Several people have not said anything and the discussion is being carried by a smaller subset.
watch_for.prevent_it: After options are on the table, explicitly invite the full group before moving to the decision block.
watch_for.if_it_happens: Pause the main thread and address the broader group with an open invitation.
watch_for.say_this: Before we move on, is there anything on the table we are missing? Any perspective we have not heard yet?

watch_for.situation: The group cannot reach agreement and the meeting risks ending without a clear next step.
watch_for.prevent_it: State both valid endings at the start so the group knows a clear decision path is also a success.
watch_for.if_it_happens: Stop trying to force agreement and shift to framing the unresolved choice precisely, then ask who has the authority to make the final call.
watch_for.say_this: We are not going to force a decision that is not there. Let us name exactly what is unresolved and figure out who can settle it and by when.

watch_for.situation: The meeting ends with an apparent agreement that is still vague enough that the next action is unclear.
watch_for.prevent_it: Reserve the last five minutes explicitly for reading back what was decided in concrete terms before anyone leaves.
watch_for.if_it_happens: Before closing, ask someone to state the decision in their own words and check whether it is specific enough to act on.
watch_for.say_this: Can someone say back what we just agreed to, specifically enough that we could put it in writing right now?

decision_plan.approach: Work through the options until one emerges that the group can accept. If there is disagreement, ask whether the objection changes the option or blocks it entirely. If a version of an option can address the objection, revise and check again. If the group is genuinely split and no resolution is in reach, the goal shifts: name the exact sticking point, capture what was agreed, and identify who has the authority to make the final call outside the room. The disagree-and-commit framing is useful here as a signal that people do not need to love the outcome to move forward with it, but do not invoke it as a mechanism to override an objection or declare the decision closed.
decision_plan.what_needs_clarifying: Who has the authority to make the final call if Sam, Priya, and the group cannot agree in the room. This should be identified before or at the start of the meeting so the group knows what a stalemate actually means.

before_the_meeting: Ask Sam and Priya separately what splits they see as workable, so you arrive knowing the range of options rather than discovering them live.
Ask Dana what aspects of the proposed splits would affect the platform group, so that impact can be raised at the right moment rather than surfacing as a surprise.
Find out who, if anyone, has the authority to make the final call if the group does not agree, and confirm whether that person is in the room.
Write the decision question somewhere visible in the room before people arrive.

before_people_leave: Read back the agreed split in specific terms, or name the exact unresolved question if agreement was not reached.
If a decision was reached, confirm who owns communicating it and to whom.
If a decision was not reached, confirm who has the authority to settle it and what the next step is.
Note anything that came up that needs a separate conversation, so it does not quietly reopen this one.
finish_strong.closing_script: Here is what we are leaving with: either a specific split we agreed on, or a precise statement of what is still open and who handles it from here. I will make sure that is written up and shared. Thank you for working through a genuinely difficult question.

cases.name: plan-bare-minimum
cases.guards: Only a goal and a duration. No invented headcount, platform, roles or lead times. No challenges selected, so watch_for is capped at 2 and may legitimately be short. This is the case that catches a model filling silence.

input.meetingGoal: Work out why the last release slipped and what we change before the next one.

meeting_plan.goal: Work out why the last release slipped and what changes before the next one.
meeting_plan.end_state: The group has named the specific causes of the slip and agreed on at least one concrete change for the next release, or the unresolved questions and who has authority to settle them are clearly written down.

agenda.title: Frame the two questions
agenda.purpose: Make sure everyone is working on the same problem before discussion opens.
agenda.how_to_run_it: State both questions plainly and write them where the group can see them: what caused the slip, and what changes before the next release. Clarify that the goal is specific answers, not a general postmortem.
agenda.say_this_if_helpful: We have 30 minutes. Two questions: what caused the slip, and what do we change before the next release. I want to leave with specific answers to both, or a clear path to them if we cannot settle everything today.

agenda.title: Causes of the slip
agenda.purpose: Surface what actually happened before moving to fixes.
agenda.how_to_run_it: Ask the group to name causes. Capture each one briefly. Where multiple causes come up, note them all rather than converging too early. If the list is growing long, ask the group to identify which causes had the most impact on the slip.
agenda.say_this_if_helpful: What do we think caused the release to slip? I will capture everything. We can sort it in a moment.

agenda.title: Agree on the changes
agenda.purpose: Turn the causes into specific, ownable changes for the next release.
agenda.how_to_run_it: For each significant cause, ask what would concretely be different next time. Push for specificity: what changes, who is involved, and by when. If the group surfaces more changes than can be resolved in the time remaining, ask which one or two matter most and flag the rest as open questions.
agenda.say_this_if_helpful: For each cause, what specifically changes before the next release? I want a clear action, not a principle.

agenda.title: Capture and close
agenda.purpose: Leave with a written record that is usable after the meeting ends.
agenda.how_to_run_it: Read back the causes named and each change agreed. For anything still unresolved, write the exact question and note who has authority to settle it if that is known. Confirm the next step for any open item.
agenda.say_this_if_helpful: Let me read back what we have. Causes: [list]. Changes agreed: [list]. Still open: [list]. Does that match what you heard?

watch_for.situation: The discussion stays on what happened and the group does not move to what changes.
watch_for.prevent_it: Write both questions visibly at the start so the shift from causes to changes is an explicit step, not an implied one.
watch_for.if_it_happens: Name the shift out loud and move the group forward.
watch_for.say_this: We have a solid picture of what happened. I want to use the time we have left on what changes. What would be different next time?

watch_for.situation: A change is agreed in words but the next action is still vague when the group moves on.
watch_for.prevent_it: For each change, ask for the specific action and who is involved before moving to the next one.
watch_for.if_it_happens: Pause and ask the clarifying question before capturing it.
watch_for.say_this: Before we move on: what specifically happens, and who is involved? I want to write something concrete.

decision_plan.approach: No decision framework was specified. For each proposed change, the group works toward a specific action. If the group agrees, write it down with enough detail to act on. If the group does not agree, write the exact unresolved question and identify who has authority to settle it before the next release.
decision_plan.what_needs_clarifying: Who has authority to approve or ratify changes if the group cannot reach agreement in the room. If that is unclear, name it as an open question before the meeting ends.

before_the_meeting: Have a way to write causes and changes where you can read them back at the end, whether that is a shared screen, a whiteboard, or notes you read aloud.
Know roughly when the next release is scheduled so you can ground any changes in a real timeline if the group asks.
If there is a short factual record of what slipped and when, have it available so the group does not spend time reconstructing the timeline from memory.

before_people_leave: Read back every cause the group named.
Read back every change agreed and the specific action attached to each one.
For anything still unresolved, write the exact question and note who can settle it if that is known.
Confirm the next step for each open item.
Ask if anything is missing before people leave.
finish_strong.closing_script: Here is what we have: [causes], [changes agreed], [open questions and next steps]. If anything looks wrong or missing, say so now. Otherwise, I will send this around so we have a shared record.

cases.name: follow-up-full-capture
cases.guards: Every section captured, and one next step deliberately has no owner and no date — it must come back with empty strings rather than a guessed owner or an invented deadline. The message must not thank anyone for contributions it cannot see or announce a next meeting nobody mentioned.

input.meetingGoal: Agree how we split on-call between the two teams for next quarter.
input.decided: Platform team takes weekday on-call, product team takes weekends, reviewed after six weeks.

nextSteps.task: Write up the six-week review criteria

input.forNextTime: We needed the incident numbers in front of us.

what_we_decided: Platform team takes weekday on-call; product team takes weekends.
The arrangement will be reviewed after six weeks.

what_happens_next.task: Write up the six-week review criteria

output.message: Here is where we landed on on-call splits for next quarter. Platform team takes weekdays, product team takes weekends, with a review after six weeks. Dana will update the rota in PagerDuty by Friday. The six-week review criteria still need to be written up — no owner was confirmed for that. We also left open the question of public holiday cover, which will need a decision before the new rota takes effect. For any future conversation on this, having the incident numbers available would help.

cases.name: follow-up-only-one-section
cases.guards: Nothing decided, no next steps — only an open question. what_we_decided and what_happens_next MUST be empty arrays. A placeholder or a guessed decision here is the exact failure the old tool shipped, which pre-generated a decision log before the meeting had happened.

input.stillOpen: We could not agree on whether the migration comes before or after the audit.

still_open: Whether the migration comes before or after the audit
output.message: We met to decide Q4 priorities. The one question we were not able to settle is whether the migration should come before or after the audit. That choice remains open. If you have input on it or know who can make the call, please share it so we can move forward.
